issue_claim: operator can declare too much yield or choose a bad settlement amount
why_it_looked_bad: yield settlement paths often move value, so a wrong proposed yield appears to create phantom surplus or drain reserves
why_not_valid: if the only failure is a trusted Operator intentionally or negligently passing bad parameters, and the contract's on-chain backing/surplus gates correctly reject states without real net backing, the issue is a trusted-role or parameter-risk claim rather than a standalone Medium/High bug
downgrade_reason: requires malicious/inactive/mistaken trusted Operator behavior without a contract-side invariant failure in the safety gate
trust_assumption: Operator or keeper is trusted or explicitly bounded by public-known contest assumptions; the relevant security property is whether contract gates independently validate net backing
when_it_could_be_real: the on-chain gate omits an asset/liability field and therefore accepts a bad settlement during normal operation
untrusted users can manipulate the gate input or trigger settlement against stale/gross-only accounting
the protocol documentation promises contract-enforced backing bounds that are bypassed by adapter accounting
